sources.note: Used for size and appearance. The Wikipedia title Large-spotted genet redirects to the Cape genet (Genetta tigrina) and was not used.

size.note: Head-and-body length (42–52 cm), tail (40–53 cm) and mass (1.3–3 kg) follow the Wikipedia account of the rusty-spotted genet, a name used there and by EWT for the large-spotted complex (often as Genetta maculata). These figures are entered with that taxonomy caveat, not as measurements published under the name Genetta fieldiana alone.

summary: A slender, nocturnal genet with fairly large, often rusty or blotched spots and a dark tail tip. In this guide it is stored as Genetta fieldiana, the Kruger large-spotted genet, distinct from the Cape genet Genetta tigrina and from the small-spotted genet Genetta felina.
description: The large-spotted genet is a lightly built viverrid with a long, ringed tail that ends in a dark tip, not a white one. The spots are larger and often rustier or more blotched than in the small-spotted genet, and the feet are the same colour as the fur rather than dark. EWT assesses the complex as the rusty-spotted genet under the name Genetta maculata, and notes that there is no mid-dorsal crest. Sexes are similar in colour. Photographs in this file are Kruger animals identified as G. fieldiana, or Kruger animals clearly showing the dark tail tip and rusty blotches.
habits: It is nocturnal, usually solitary, and often partly arboreal. It is frequently seen after dark on paths and around rest camps in Kruger, including in trees and on camp paving.

diet.summary: An opportunistic feeder, taking small vertebrates, insects and fruit. A Kruger-specific diet study was not found in the sources consulted.

young: The EWT 2025 assessment, citing Skinner and Chimimba (2005), gives a breeding peak in October to December, with a possible second peak in March to May, and litters of 2–5 kittens. A Kruger-specific account beyond that regional description was not found.
habitat: Woodland, riverine trees and the edges of rest camps. It is widespread in Kruger and is the large-spotted genet most often recorded in the park.

similar.note: The small-spotted genet has smaller, neater spots, dark feet, a dark chin, and a white tail tip rather than a dark one.
The African civet is much larger and heavier, with a deep chest, a bold black-and-white face and black legs.

research.note: No Kruger population figure was found. Size follows rusty-spotted genet sources, which use the name Genetta maculata; that caveat is in the size note. iNaturalist taxon 1643992 (Genetta fieldiana) was preferred for photographs. One Bernard DUPONT Kruger photograph, labelled Genetta maculata, was included because it is a Kruger animal at Tamboti and clearly shows the dark tail tip. The Wikipedia article Large-spotted genet, which redirects to the Cape genet, was not used. No reusable Kruger recording was found. The stored Afrikaans name Rooikolmuskejaatkat is the 2011 checklist name.

gaps: No Kruger population figure was found.
No size figures published under the name Genetta fieldiana alone were found; the ranges entered are from rusty-spotted genet accounts.
A general field description of the calls was not found in the sources consulted.
Iris colour, ear colour and underpart colour were not given as named values in the sources used, so those marks are null.
